issue.title: Cycler Task-Link close stays pending >30 s without opening the successor picker in a freshly launched scratch Obsidian
issue.description:
Proposed by bob-cli-k7.6 note #2 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP), triaged by the bob-cli-k7 land agent.

During the k7.6 real-vault audit (isolated scratch Obsidian 1.15.0 under xvfb-run, scratch clone of the Bob vault at snapshot d5d358c4, synced bob-plugins: task-status-cycler 1.49.0, bob-ledger-tools 1.110.0, bob-navigation-hotkeys with api.successors v4 and pick present), the cycler's Task-Link close `handleActiveTaskBlockLinkOpenDone` on `[[job_email_recruiters#^bryan-stephen-luzern-risk]]` completed the task and the ledger row was struck. But the close promise was still `{pending: true}` after 30 s, and `successors.pick` was never called, so the `Keep ‹job_email_recruiters› moving` picker never opened. Audit artifact: file:explicit:f5ddb7ad06ac2f48744b7d06 (picker.closeResult pending, pickerModels []).

The plan side is correct. On the same scratch vault, `bob capture --dry-run` and the rendered ⏭ 4 mark agree on the four-row identity set. A new node test drives the identical close through the real wiring with a fake nav picker and opens exactly that 4-row group: `KM33: Ctrl+Enter on the screenshot link opens a 4-row Keep group and Esc writes nothing` in bob-plugins scripts/test-task-status-cycler-keep-moving.cjs, added in the k7 landing. So the stall is somewhere between `finalizeClosedTasks` → `planAndApplySuccessorsNow` and the picker call, in a real, freshly launched Obsidian.

Unconfirmed suspects, in plugins/task-status-cycler/src/137-plugin-successor-project.js:
- `buildSuccessorPool` falling back to `readSuccessorColdDocuments`, a full-vault cold read, while Tasks is not yet Warm in a just-launched Obsidian. X carries an [id::], so needsDependents is true.
- `readSuccessorRelationInputs` / the relation preflight waiting on ledger-tools' relation index, since relations.successor_labels is configured.
- An earlier queued mutation holding `referenceMutationQueue`.

Note that the strike may come from reference retirement inside finalizeClosedTasks, not from the post-finalize strike. That would mean planAndApplySuccessorsNow returned and the wait is later, in presentSuccessorModel or the notice.

First establish whether this reproduces in Bryan's warm, long-running Obsidian; it may be specific to a cold, just-launched scratch instance. If it reproduces anywhere real, a Ctrl+Enter whose successor picker appears 30 s+ late (or never) is a user-visible defect for every close that plans successors, not only keep-moving.

task_type_fields.impact: A Ctrl+Enter whose successor picker opens 30 s+ late or never would hide every successor offer (hand-offs, relation successors, keep-moving) for that close; so far observed only in a cold scratch Obsidian.
task_type_fields.repro: Build an isolated scratch vault from a clone of the Bob vault (never ~/bob), sync bob-plugins into it, and launch Obsidian under `xvfb-run -a` with Tasks `taskFormat: dataview`. The bob-plugins harness `scripts/obsidian-keep-moving-marks-e2e{,-lib}.cjs` shows the launch pattern. Open today's daily note, place the cursor on a live Task Link into a leaf project with Ready/Next residents (e.g. job_email_recruiters at snapshot d5d358c4), and run the cycler's Task-Link close (Ctrl+Enter / handleActiveTaskBlockLinkOpenDone). Observe whether `api.successors.pick` is called and whether the close promise settles within 30 s. Instrument planAndApplySuccessorsNow phases with timestamps to locate the stall.

issue.creation_reason: The bob-cli-k7 audit could not observe the Keep-moving picker opening in real Obsidian: the Task-Link close stayed pending more than 30 s without calling successors.pick, while node-level wiring tests open the picker correctly. This needs its own investigation of the successor pass's real-Obsidian latency.

payload.description: Keep-moving marks epic whose real-vault audit (k7.6) observed the stalled close; its ⏭ mark promises the picker this bead must make open
